quotes.label: The cabin entrance
quotes.quote: After Frankenstein’s death, the Monster boards Walton’s ship and looks over his former enemy. He begins a monologue reflecting on his entire life. Nietzsche writes that Nihilism comes from searching for “a purpose which is not there: so that the seeker will ultimately lose courage” and that “Nihilism is therefore the coming into consciousness of the long waste of strength” (Nietzsche 16).
quotes.analysis: The Monster’s Monologue reveals that he has lost his sense of Purpose, completing the last stage of psychological Nihilism. Nietzsche demonstrates that even if for a long time someone believes they have a defined purpose, they may fall into Nihilism if that purpose is upended.

quotes.label: Frankenstien’s Body
quotes.quote: The Monster reflects on destroying Frankenstein’s hopes, yet “not [satisfying] [his] own desires” that were “ardent and craving” (Shelley 165). Regretting that he was “still spurned” from “love and fellowship” (Shelley 165).
quotes.analysis: These reflections signify the collapse of purpose. With his superficial goal having been completed, the Monster realizes that it was never going to make him feel better. Understanding that his true passions were impossible to fulfill, he sees that his torturing of Frankenstein was a “long waste of strength.”

quotes.label: The Monster’s face
quotes.quote: The Monster continues by stating that Walton’s "abhorrence cannot equal that with which [the Monster] [regards] [himself],” highlighting the Monster’s lack of self-worth (Shelley 165).
quotes.analysis: The Monster’s feeling of “abhorrence” reflects Nietzsche's writings that Nihilism can manifest as a “shame in one’s own presence”‘ (Nietzsche 16). The Monster’s disdain for himself reveals his transition to Nihilism.

quotes.label: The opening towards the arctic
quotes.quote: The Monster ends by deciding to end his life, remarking that he will “no longer see the sun or stars, or feel the winds play on [his] cheek” (Shelley 166).
quotes.analysis: Deciding to lose the very things that originally brought him joy when he first came into existence, the very things that have been a constant beacon of support through his life, reveals how the Monster has fully transitioned into Nihilism.
